reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads Genesis 26 not as a new naming but as Isaac restoring a name Abraham gave a century earlier, lapsed after the Philistines stopped up the well.

discrepancy.note: Strauss cites Beersheba, like the naming of Isaac and Jacob, as an Old Testament case where two rival narrators' explanations of the same fact were later fused into one book.

quotes.text: That different narrators may give different explanations of the same fact, and that these different explanations may afterwards be united in one book, is proved by many examples in the O. T. Thus in Genesis, three derivations are given of the name of Isaac; two of that of Jacob (xxv. 26., xxvii. 16), and so of Edom and Beersheba (xxi. 31., xxvi. 33).
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, note 145 (1846), on Genesis 21:31 and Genesis 26:33.
